title: Tensor-invertible modules over unique factorization domains are trivial
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain with unique factorization: every nonzero nonunit is a finite product of prime elements, uniquely up to order and multiplication by units. Let $N$ be an $R$-module, and write $N^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R)$. Use tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If the evaluation map $N^\vee\otimes_RN\to R$, $\varphi\otimes n\mapsto\varphi(n)$, is bijective, then there is an $R$-linear isomorphism $N\cong R$.
